Prevention: Rotate tobacco with maize, groundnuts, etc. and come back with tobacco after 4 years
Use certified seed and resistant varieties e.g.
Uproot and burn tobacco stalks after reaping (harvesting)
Remove alternative hosts like tomatoes, potatoes and eggplant.
Keep the field weed-free to avoid harbouring the disease
Avoid fields that have a history of fusarium wilt
Solarize the soil in the nursery for 8 weeks to kill the fungal spores
Ensure good field hygiene/sanitation to minimise infection - sterilise tools, reduce movement of soil
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: tomatoes, bananas, potato
Look for yellowing, wilting plants which tilt on one side 4 weeks after transplanting
Look for stunting and premature death of plants
Uproot suspected plants and cut the stem length ways.
If there is brown staining inside the stem the plant is infected
Carry out green direct controls if 2 to 3 plants per 0.4ha are infected by the pathogen
Direct Control: Uproot and burn all infected plants
Restrictions: There are currently no effective chemical controls for this disease
